verdict:
V2B attempt 1: ACCEPTED WITH CONDITIONS. Reviewer: external (operator relay).
B0, B1, B2, B3, B5 (reference, kernel, noise parity, decoder, body) and B7 are
accepted. B4 and the B5 encoder are accepted with required fixes. The B6 dry
run is recorded as a FAILED DRY RUN THAT FOUND DEFECTS, not as model evidence.
Its "inverted looming control" and "all rows silent" outcomes are caused by
implementation and design defects, not by the circuit:
D1 encoding_v2.py swaps the populations: LC4 receives angular size and LPLC2
   receives expansion. Plan v2 and Ache et al. 2019 require LC4 = expansion
   (angular velocity) and LPLC2 = angular size.
D2 Expansion is not normalized. It is in rad/ms and about 50 times smaller
   than angular size in rad, so expansion contributes almost nothing.
D3 The dry-run looming stimulus continues at full size after impact for the rest
   of the trial, and the matched non-looming control applies full final size
   from t = 0. The control therefore receives more drive for longer.
D4 Noise and synaptic scale grids are orders of magnitude too small. With
   p = 0.01 per tick and w = 0.05 the steady free membrane potential is about
   0.005 of threshold. One contact at scale 0.003 gives a peak PSP of about
   0.0005 of threshold, so multi-hop signals cannot propagate.
D5 The draft criterion "looming escape exceeds non-looming by 0.10" is also an
   H1 outcome metric. Calibrating on an outcome is circular.
D6 The draft criteria contain no false-escape limit.
D7 atan_approx has about 5.8% relative error at small angles (slope 1.058 at 0).
D8 The u32 mixer combines all counters linearly before a single finalizer, so
   (tick, index) pairs can collide along lattice lines.
Reviewer decisions on V2B questions are in C1, C2 and C4 of the V2C prompt.
